rites.name: Tiravaloma
rites.text: Tiravaloma is the concept of a resonant hum that drew the first roots of Gukornok together during the Singing, when no clock yet counted time. In the Age of Strangers, traders who anchored their boats to it learned its tone and carried that tone away with their goods.

rites.name: Analamrauta
rites.text: Analamrauta is a concept of Gukornok, a principle of binding oaths that the Courts of the Second Era used to hold rival powers to their word. It was less a being than a rule the trials invoked when a witness's pledge had to hold against the weight of landfall.

rites.name: Syazis
rites.text: Syazis is a concept from Gukornok's Walled Age, a principle that a city's wall is only as strong as the oaths sworn beside it. Its adherents in the Grounded Realm hold that a stone wall remembers every hand that built it, and that holding a line for centuries is itself a kind of power. The concept is expressed through rites of stone-setting and vigil rather than any great blow.

rites.name: Silimioniel
rites.text: Silimioniel is a concept of Gukornok born in the Walled Age, when cities raised holding walls and orders of stone-wardens kept the old roads. Its power rests on the idea of a threshold that must be crossed carefully, and it grew strongest during the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke ancient bonds between towns.

rites.name: Nontium
rites.text: A tuning craft lets a rider quicken forward motion or briefly lift off the ground. It can also slow a vehicle or shift its drive, and it only pushes toward the front, so backward rushes need impacts or evasive swerves.
